claims.claim_text: The indexed Timothy R. Marsh is the Tennessee-born Coyne graduate, civilian Signal Corps radio operator, and OSS communications instructor documented by the National Park Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact first and last name, middle initial supplied in the NPS source note, civilian status, radio specialty, Chicago chronology, and Area C instructor role align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact indexed name plus the NPS source note's middle initial and multiple distinctive civilian and OSS identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history sequences his 1941 move, Coyne graduation, civilian Signal Corps work, November 1943 OSS recruitment, and December 1943 Area C assignment.
claims.match_notes: Box 485 remains unreviewed. The blank index rank and serial fields are compatible with the official history's explicit civilian status.

claims.claim_text: Marsh's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was civilian employment with the United States Army Signal Corps.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says he worked as a civilian Signal Corps radio operator after Coyne and was recruited by an OSS-employed former instructor in November 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, middle-initial, civilian-radio, and Area C instructor match.
claims.match_notes: The Signal Corps is a military organization, but Marsh's relationship is explicitly civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: The Army Signal Corps is Marsh's last identified civilian employer before OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official chronology places civilian Signal Corps employment directly before his OSS recruitment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same official biographical sequence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly sequenced as the last civilian job before OSS.
claims.match_notes: This civilian relationship is not mislabeled as military service.

claims.claim_text: Before working for the Signal Corps, Marsh attended and graduated from Coyne Radio School in Chicago.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS identifies Coyne training before the civilian Signal Corps job.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name and documented radio-instructor chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student affiliation, not the immediate predecessor to OSS.
claims.match_notes: Coyne is not presented as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Colonel Lawrence W. Lowman is Lawrence Wise Lowman, the CBS operations executive appointed chief of the OSS Communications Branch.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, full middle-name expansion, colonel grade, branch-chief position, and cited 1942 recruitment records align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact indexed name plus matching grade and a uniquely specific OSS command assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS cites recruitment and clearance records from May to June 1942 and the Communications Branch's formal creation in September 1942.
claims.match_notes: Box 465 remains unreviewed; the index's Colonel grade is compatible with the official branch-chief account.

claims.claim_text: Lowman's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Columbia Broadcasting System.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS identifies him as CBS vice president in charge of operations and says he was named chief of the newly unified OSS Communications Branch.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, grade, and OSS command match.
claims.match_notes: The historical CBS name and executive title are preserved.

claims.claim_text: CBS is Lowman's last documented civilian employer before his OSS appointment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official account directly sequences his CBS operations vice presidency and appointment as OSS Communications Branch chief.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name and branch-chief chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly date-bounded to the 1942 OSS appointment.
claims.match_notes: No intervening civilian employer is documented in the reviewed official recruitment chronology.

claims.claim_text: The indexed John M. Balsamo is probably the civilian OSS Morse-code instructor and former Wall Street telegrapher described by the National Park Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact first and last name and compatible civilian status align, but the official narrative omits the middle initial and no personnel file has been reviewed.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable rather than high confidence because the source supplies no corroborating middle initial, birth detail, employer name, or unique service number.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source places Wall Street telegraph work before wartime civilian instruction at OSS Area C but gives no exact dates.
claims.match_notes: Box 33 must be reviewed before treating this as a settled identity. The separate Ferdinand A. Balsamo row is not merged or used as evidence.

claims.claim_text: If the probable identity match is correct, Balsamo had worked as a telegrapher on Wall Street before his OSS instructional work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS documents the occupation and location but does not name a bank, brokerage, exchange, or telegraph company.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable identity; the employment statement is not published as an unqualified fact.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented before OSS Area C service, but the dates and immediate sequence are not established.
claims.match_notes: No reliable named pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Colonel William R. Peers is William Ray Peers, the infantry officer selected for the original OSS Detachment 101 cadre.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, Ray name variant, compatible officer-grade progression, first Detachment 101 cadre, and Peers's later first-person account align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact indexed name plus military grade, infantry specialty, distinctive Detachment 101 command history, and participant-authored institutional account.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS places the selection and first OSS training in April 1942; the CIA hosts Peers's own later history of Detachment 101.
claims.match_notes: Box 593 remains unreviewed. The full service number is never shown publicly.

claims.claim_text: Peers's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was probably commissioned service in the United States Army.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS identifies him as an infantry lieutenant selected by another Army officer for the original Detachment 101 cadre in early 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name and Detachment 101 match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate military pathway; the exact prior unit and transfer order remain to be checked in Box 593.
claims.match_notes: Army service is not classified as a civilian employer, and no civilian-employer claim is made.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Major Nicol Smith is the prewar travel writer and OSS Free Thai mission leader documented by the National Park Service and CIA.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact unusual given-name form, compatible major grade, early 1942 OSS entry, Area B training, Far East experience, and Free Thai leadership align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the rare exact name plus matching grade, early OSS training, occupation, and uniquely specific mission assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS places his OSS entry in early 1942 and Area B training in April; CIA independently describes him as a former travel writer and Donovan recruit.
claims.match_notes: Box 724 remains unreviewed. The NPS article's occasional 'Nichol' spelling is retained as a documented variant rather than silently substituted.

claims.claim_text: Smith's best-supported immediate pre-OSS civilian affiliation was self-employment as a travel writer and author.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS describes him as a successful prewar author and dates OSS entry to early 1942; CIA calls him a former travel writer and Donovan personal recruit.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the rare-name, grade, and Free Thai mission match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to early 1942, though neither source supplies a last day of civilian work.
claims.match_notes: His publishers are not inferred to be employers; the relationship is modeled as self-employment.

claims.claim_text: Self-employed travel writing is Smith's last documented civilian work before OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two institutional histories identify the writing occupation immediately before or in direct connection with his early 1942 recruitment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same rare-name and mission chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded, with no intervening civilian employer identified.
claims.match_notes: The claim is self-employment, not employment by Bobbs-Merrill or another publisher.

research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the named civilian Signal Corps employer and kept Coyne student status separate from employment.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 485 for precise civilian employment and OSS contract dates.
